defects.detail: opening word fragment 'rentissimum' (most flourishing) is dropped; translation begins ', yet hitherto unknown'
'vera forma salutari nondum meretur' (does not yet deserve to be called a true form) rendered 'does not yet deserve the name of true salutary form'

reason: Drops the fragment 'rentissimum' and misreads 'salutari' as 'salutary'; XV and XVI otherwise match the source closely.
Questions VII-X and the end of VI are rendered accurately, including the univocal/analogical distinction and the species definition; nothing wrong found.
The Mandraite speech, the parting at Myus and the temple statue all match the source; the Pyrrha note is accurate.

defects.detail: opening fragment 'influxio.' is rendered as a spurious margin '<margin>Influx</margin>' plus 'fluxion.'

reason: The Caraña properties, the Cartagena variety and the castor-oil extraction and uses are all rendered faithfully; the only problem is a spurious margin made from the word fragment 'influxio'.

defects.detail: source 'gratia compositi; quorum primus...' (end of the Latin title, 'composed for the sake of [the French...]') becomes 'The second volume of these dialogues was published for the first time as *The Spirit of the Composed* <note>original Latin: *Spiritus, gratia compositi*</note>', an invented title and an invented 'original'

reason: Invents a title, 'The Spirit of the Composed', and a fake Latin original for 'gratia compositi'; the Cabinet, Mirouer and Socinus entries are otherwise faithful.

defects.detail: summary says the author 'dismisses as a poor imitation' and discusses 'late development of astronomical terms'; source says only 'Ein wertloses Machwerk' and nothing about imitation
'εὐθηλῆ' transliterated as 'euthylē'

reason: Notes 6-17 and the Artemis introduction match the German; the summary adds an 'imitation' claim the source does not make, and one Greek word is mis-transliterated.

defects.detail: column 1 of this page ('οἱ ἕκαστον τῶν ὄντων...') is wrapped in '<meta>continues from previous page: ...', which mislabels this page's own text as previous-page text

summary asserts 'Proclus explores ... the role of analogy, geometry, and proportionality in the Demiurge's work'; the garbled page names Timaeus but supports no such coherent argument and never names the Demiurge

reason: The source is heavily garbled OCR (dozens of 'ᾗ'); the translation glosses it word for word and marks the garble as <unclear>, so it is faithful to the OCR but unreadable. It mislabels column 1 as previous-page text and the summary overstates coherence. The Greek is read only weakly.

defects.detail: opening '<meta>continues from previous page: ...could I see anything because I was held back by fear and lack of understanding.</meta>' has no counterpart on this page; it completes the previous page's 'ne per me sopotea' with invented content
'Mitrauagliaua' (troubled/afflicted me) rendered 'Made me wonder' in the verse and 'I WAS WONDERING' in the lemma
'secondo che scriue Luca al. xxiii. cap.' rendered 'Luke writes in the 24th chapter'
'e/ translatione dalle biade' (a metaphor from grain) rendered 'It is a translation from grain'

reason: Invents a sentence finishing the previous page, renders 'mi travagliava' as 'made me wonder', changes Luke xxiii to 24 and gives 'translatione' as 'translation'; the canto argument, verses and Samaritan gloss are otherwise faithful.

defects.detail: 'والعوضة اسفل منه ... تعلق العوضة ابدا الى اسفل' (the wound's cavity/opening should hang downward) rendered 'the healing process is below it ... the healing process always attaches downwards', and labelled as previous-page text
'ويجب ان يعتدي المريض ... بغير ذا محو حسن الكثرة' (the patient should be fed well) rendered 'to avoid excessive movement'
'ونيادي الى العشي' (leads to fainting, الغشي) rendered 'leading to emaciation'
final 'وارضا' (likely وايضا, 'also') rendered 'and satisfaction'

reason: The opening lines on wound drainage become 'healing process' nonsense and a garbled dietary instruction becomes 'avoid excessive movement'; the passages on flesh regeneration, the dangerous arm and knee wounds and amputation broadly match. The handwritten Arabic OCR is read only moderately.

defects.detail: 'Iß Theil deß Vorwinters' (This part of the pre-winter) rendered 'In the part of the pre-winter'

reason: The date and time, ascendant, midheaven and planetary positions, the deferral clause and the closing note on weather all match the source.

defects.detail: XXXII source ends '...sine caeterorum' with the main verb on the next page ('non potest ita credere'); translation imports 'cannot lend money ... without the consent of the other'

reason: XXVIII-XXXI and their legal citations, expanded in notes, are faithful; XXXII imports the main verb 'cannot lend' from the next page.
The mechanism of prepared antimony with a purgans, the plea for a longer life and the broken second column, kept as <unclear> fragments, all match the source.

defects.detail: 'Prodit Augustus Orientis Imperator Maximinus, facundiâ et majestate, ...' loses 'facundiâ et majestate' (with eloquence and majesty)
opening fragment 'fuetos.' (end of 'assuetos', accustomed) rendered 'deeds.'
the address 'A.A.' in 'veritatis nucleum eruamus A.A.' is dropped

reason: Drops 'facundiâ et majestate' and 'A.A.' and renders the fragment 'fuetos' as 'deeds'; the conversion of the Empress and Porphyrius, the laurel allegory and the martyrdom are otherwise faithful.

defects.detail: 'on tire son souphre montel' (garbled word) rendered 'one draws out its celestial sulfur'

'marcassites, ematites, dilates et animés par ce esprit' (sulfurs dilated and animated by this spirit) treats 'dilates' as a further substance, 'dilates <gloss>expanded substances</gloss>, and animated'
'souphres tifs' glossed as 'volatile principles', which the source does not support

reason: Renders 'souphre montel' as 'celestial sulfur' and treats 'dilates' as a list item; the double mercury, living sulfur, work of the poor and regenerated gold steps otherwise match.
